//: demo/ holds ordinary application-code fixtures (the jest/React world) plus the ava test infrastructure --
the opposite of test/, which is the acceptance-suite world. So unlike test/tsconfig.json there are no
mocha or @wdio/globals types here: their absence is part of what makes these fixtures ordinary.
jest's types are not named either, deliberately: jest is not a dependency of this package (the lint-side
version comes from `settings.jest.version` in the root .eslintrc.js), so `types: ["jest"]` would not
resolve. The only ambient types the demo world needs are node's, for the ava infrastructure under
Nothing runs `tsc -p demo` in the build, and it would not pass if something did: example.ts deliberately
violates rules (implicit anys, unused locals) to exercise the ESLint side. This file exists so an editor
opens the demo fixtures with honest compiler assumptions instead of inheriting none at all.
